title: Sort records
prompt: Return a new array of the tasks, sorted by priority from smallest to largest. Tasks with the same priority are sorted by title, A to Z. Leave the array you were given unchanged. Use the built-in sort with a comparator.
hints: What should the comparator return when two priorities differ, and what when they are equal?
Return the difference of the priorities. When it is 0, compare the titles.
Copy first with [...tasks]. Compare titles with < and >, returning -1, 1 or 0.
checks: __same(sortTasks([{ title: "write", priority: 2 }, { title: "call", priority: 1 }, { title: "plan", priority: 2 }]).map(task => task.title), ["call", "plan", "write"])
(() => { const input = [{ title: "b", priority: 2 }, { title: "a", priority: 1 }]; sortTasks(input); return input[0].title === "b"; })()
checkLabels: Priority 1 comes first. Within priority 2, plan comes before write.
No tasks give an empty array.
Priorities are compared as numbers: 9 comes before 10.
The array you were given must not change.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Compares priorities and leaves equal ones in the order they arrived.
Sorts the caller's array instead of a copy.

feedback: A comparator answers one question about two items: which comes first? Decide that for different priorities, then for equal ones.
